analysis.investment_thesis: Action Construction Equipment is a rare Indian industrial compounder — ROCE of 40.1%, revenue CAGR of 20.2% over 9 years, net profit CAGR of 52.8%, nearly debt-free, and trading at only 25.8x earnings with margins still expanding. As India's dominant pick-and-carry crane manufacturer, ACE sits at the intersection of the country's decade-long infrastructure supercycle.
key_strengths: ROCE of 40.1% is world-class for a capital-equipment manufacturer and has been achieved while growing revenue at 20%+ — this is not a one-year aberration but a structural advantage

Extreme operating leverage: EBITDA margins expanded from ~6.6% in FY16 to 16.9% in FY25 as fixed costs were absorbed across a much larger revenue base, with operating income growing at 36.4% CAGR vs revenue at 20.2%
Essentially debt-free (D/E 0.08) with INR 412 Cr operating cash flow in FY25 — the balance sheet is self-funding and management has not needed external capital to grow
key_risks: Construction equipment is deeply cyclical; a slowdown in government infrastructure spending (roads, metro, real estate) would hit revenues rapidly with high fixed-cost leverage cutting both ways
Rising capex (INR 221 Cr in FY25 vs INR 48 Cr in FY22) and recent borrowing uptick (INR 143 Cr) suggest expansion is accelerating — execution risk increases with scale
FCF declined to INR 206 Cr in FY25 from INR 268 Cr in FY24 despite profit growth, as capex consumed more cash — investors must monitor whether ROIC holds at elevated capex
red_flags: Promoter holding at 65.42% is healthy but DII holding of only 1.76% suggests domestic institutional under-ownership — could indicate valuation concerns among sophisticated local investors
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Munger's first test: is this a business I can understand? Yes. ACE makes cranes. India is building roads, metro systems, ports, airports, and factories at a scale not seen in a generation. You need cranes to build all of it. ACE has built the dominant position in pick-and-carry cranes — a category where they have 50%+ market share — through superior after-sales service networks and cost-efficient manufacturing. ROCE of 40% proves the moat is real, not imagined. The nine-year financial record is a beautiful thing: revenue, operating income, EBITDA, net profit, and FCF all moving steadily upward with compounding acceleration.

The valuation at 25.8x trailing earnings is not cheap in absolute terms, but it is honest relative to the growth rate. A business growing earnings at 50%+ per year with 40% ROCE and zero debt deserves a premium multiple. My principal concern is whether elevated capex (INR 382 Cr investing outflows in FY25) will sustain these returns or dilute them — the next two years will answer that. The management has earned the benefit of the doubt through consistent, capital-efficient execution over nearly a decade. At this price, you are getting a quality compounder at a fair price — and that is precisely the Berkshire formula.
